objectives.wording: Use dated Indian data to compare common malignancies and distinguish inherited and modifiable risks.
Compare presentation, progression and complications of representative malignancies.
Elicit, document and present a cancer history covering risk factors, symptom duration and evolution to help establish the aetiology.
Demonstrate general and focused examination and document clues to local extent, spread and complications.
Demonstrate breast, rectal and cervical examination and cervical cytology sampling on models.
Prioritize malignant and nonmalignant explanations for a simulated presentation.
Select and interpret representative blood counts, faecal occult blood and PSA results in clinical context.
Using a supplied case, explain how the patient's needs and preferences shape the choice between curative and palliative therapy.
Explain how representative germline and somatic alterations contribute to cancer.
Link representative infections to malignancies and explain mechanisms and prevention opportunities.
Identify common physical and psychosocial concerns and explain person-centred care priorities.
Distinguish treatment goals and explain when palliative care can accompany disease-directed therapy.
Compare pharmacological and nonpharmacological approaches to common symptoms and distress.
Describe indications for and interpret chest radiography, mammography, skin and tissue biopsies, and tumour markers used in common cancers.
Use structured assessment to document pain intensity, function and other sources of distress.
Describe the indications, use and adverse effects of opioid analgesics for cancer pain.
Compare indications for surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy in representative cancers.
Match preventive interventions and screening tests to appropriate groups and explain their benefits and limitations.
Use applicable guidance to analyze consent, decision-making and treatment limits in a simulated case.
Define and measure obesity in the Indian population context.
Define and measure obesity in the Indian population context.
Compare modifiable and nonmodifiable risks and identify clues to secondary causes.
Compare modifiable and nonmodifiable risks and identify clues to secondary causes.
Explain how food access, eating patterns, work and physical activity influence population risk.
Connect progression to representative metabolic, mechanical and psychosocial complications.
Elicit, document and present a history covering obesity course, diet, modifiable risks, family history, clues to secondary causes and motivation for weight loss.

Perform, document and demonstrate a history-guided physical examination including general examination, measurement of abdominal obesity, and assessment for signs of secondary causes and comorbidities.
Prioritize likely causes from representative symptoms and examination findings.
Select and interpret tests for comorbidities and suspected secondary causes.
Select and interpret targeted tests when findings suggest a secondary cause.
Agree on feasible behavioural, dietary and activity changes with a simulated patient.
Explore barriers without judgment and revise a simulated care plan collaboratively.
Adapt prevention messages for patients, health workers and the public.
Recognize presentations suggesting a single-gene cause and explain representative mechanisms.
Compare indications, drug mechanisms and adverse effects and explain bariatric eligibility and risks.
Classify common upper and lower sources and identify representative risk factors.
Explain assessment and stabilization priorities for acute blood loss in simulation.
Elicit and present route, quantity, duration, symptoms of volume loss, comorbidities and risks.
Demonstrate general and abdominal examination and document volume status.
Use clinical findings to estimate the source and recognize exceptions.
Prioritize likely and dangerous causes from supplied findings.
Select and interpret blood counts, coagulation, stool, liver and H. pylori tests where indicated.
Present a simulated plan covering resuscitation, transfusion and haemostasis.
Use haemodynamic findings and response to initial care to justify the level and urgency of referral.
Discuss the suspected cause and treatment options empathetically with a simulated patient and family.
Explain the physiological consequences of acute blood loss and haemorrhagic shock.
Demonstrate consent, positioning and anal and rectal examination on a mannequin.
Enumerate indications for endoscopy, colonoscopy and relevant imaging investigations in a scenario of suspected upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
Identify when endoscopic or surgical intervention is indicated.
Compare component and whole blood indications and explain recognition and management of a suspected incompatible transfusion.
Observe compatibility testing and transfusion and document key safety checks.
Explain the indications, relevant pharmacology and adverse effects of vasopressors used in the treatment of upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
Compare acid suppression and H. pylori eradication strategies by indication, mechanism and adverse effects.
Compare infectious and noninfectious causes of acute and chronic diarrhoea.
Explain dehydration, electrolyte disturbance and systemic effects.
Relate persistent symptoms and malabsorption to nutritional and systemic effects.
Elicit and present course, diet, travel, sexual exposures and coexisting illness.
Demonstrate assessment of hydration, systemic findings and the abdomen.
Prioritize likely and serious causes using a simulated presentation.
Select and interpret blood counts and stool findings where indicated.
Decide when stool or blood culture is warranted in a simulated acute case.
Justify serology, colonoscopy, imaging and biopsy using clinical clues.
Compare indication, mechanism and harms of cause-directed treatment, including immune therapies when appropriate.
Distinguish clinical patterns and explain how they guide evaluation.
Identify common parasitic forms on supplied stool microscopy.
Identify Vibrio cholerae in a hanging-drop specimen under supervision.
Compare indications, actions and harms of representative therapies by organism.
Compare supportive and organism-specific treatment and explain indications and adverse effects of medicines.
Distinguish representative presentations and explain findings that guide further evaluation.
Identify indications for surgery and explain how the role differs between Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis.
Define and classify headache and describe the presenting features and precipitating, aggravating and relieving factors of its various types.
Elicit, document and present a headache history including aura, precipitating, aggravating and relieving factors, and associated symptoms that help identify the cause.
Demonstrate examination for focal deficits, raised intracranial pressure and meningeal signs.
Generate, document and present a differential diagnosis for headache based on the clinical features.
Select and interpret representative tests and imaging based on clinical findings.
Identify admission and escalation criteria and explain immediate supportive measures.
Discuss lifestyle measures and preventive treatment with a simulated patient who has migraine or tension-type headache.
Distinguish migraine with and without aura and recognize representative variants.
Compare indications, actions, dosing principles and adverse effects of representative preventive medicines.
Explain when lumbar puncture is appropriate and compare CSF patterns across meningitis types.
Demonstrate preparation, positioning, sampling and safety checks on a mannequin.
Interpret opening pressure, cell count, glucose, protein and microbiology in sample reports.
Compare indications, actions, dosing principles and adverse effects using a current reference.
Describe the pharmacology, doses, adverse reactions and regimens of medicines used for bacterial, tuberculous and viral meningitis.
Map major arterial territories to brain functions and representative deficits.
Classify ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke and compare mechanisms and inherited and acquired risks.
Elicit, document and present a cerebrovascular history including onset, progression, precipitating, aggravating and relieving factors, and associated symptoms that help identify the cause.
Demonstrate and document a focused general and neurological examination in simulation.
Distinguish upper and lower motor neuron patterns and infer the side, site and likely nature of the lesion.
Choose and interpret imaging to identify stroke type, site and likely cause.
Select and interpret targeted investigations based on representative risk factors and presentation.
Explain immediate assessment, supportive care and escalation in simulation.
Use applicable guidance to explain management and thrombolysis eligibility, contraindications and escalation.
Explain stabilization, monitoring and specialist management priorities in a simulated case.
Enumerate indications for surgery in haemorrhagic stroke.
Enumerate and describe the indications and modalities of multidisciplinary stroke rehabilitation.
Explain diagnosis, treatment, prognosis and recovery uncertainty empathetically to a simulated patient and family.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of stroke in older adults.
Examine speech and language and recognise aphasia and dysarthria.
Compare storage and voiding disturbances and relate them to neurological localization.
Explain their role, indications, timing considerations and contraindications in ischaemic stroke.
Map cortical, basal ganglia and cerebellar circuits to motor functions.
Classify movements by distribution, rhythm, repetition and modifying factors.
Elicit, document and present a movement-disorder history including onset, progression, precipitating, aggravating and relieving factors, and associated symptoms that help identify the cause.
Demonstrate and document general and neurological examination using an appropriate rating scale.
Generate, document and present a differential diagnosis for a movement disorder using history and physical examination findings.
Document the likely anatomical site, nature and cause of a representative disorder.
Select and interpret imaging based on the suspected cause and explain limitations.
Compare indications for surgery and botulinum toxin in representative disorders.
Compare drug actions, dosing principles, adverse effects and interactions using a current reference.
Define and differentiate seizures, convulsions and epilepsy.
Classify epilepsy by aetiology and discuss its pathophysiology, clinical evaluation, recognition of different types, diagnosis and diagnostic tests.
Demonstrate seizure first aid and explain recovery precautions and when to seek emergency help.
Compare antiseizure medicines by clinical use, patient factors and interactions.
Use an approved protocol to explain stabilization, reversible causes and escalation for a simulated ongoing seizure.
Enumerate local venomous snakes and describe the distinguishing marks of each.
Demonstrate field measures and teach safe transport and avoidance of harmful interventions.
Prioritize airway, breathing, circulation and escalation in a simulated envenomation.
Elicit, document and present a snakebite history covering circumstances, timing, snake type if known and symptom evolution.
